title: Hybrid Slab Sensitivity & Hiring Velocity — Q4 2027
content:
Purpose:
To evaluate a hybrid slab pricing product (mix of committed slabs + burst pricing) impact on unit economics and the headcount hiring cadence under three pricing elasticity scenarios. This sheet is the working model to inform Q4 hiring gates and a potential mid-quarter slab tilt.

Quick summary (executive):
- Proposed hybrid: 3-tier committed slabs (Starter 10k/mo, Growth 100k/mo, Scale 1M/mo) + burst price 2.5x baseline.
- Primary levers: slab discount depth, slab uptake (% customers migrating from pay-as-you-go), burst multiplier, headcount hiring velocity (SWE infra, SRE, Sales AE/CS).
- Outcome: at baseline uptake (18%), blended unit margin improves by ~4.3ppt; downside (8% uptake) margin compresses by ~2.1ppt and requires ~6-week hiring freeze for non-critical infra roles.

Model assumptions (inputs):
- Baseline list price per 1k tokens: $0.06 (generation), $0.015 (embedding).
- Slab discounts: Starter 15% off, Growth 35% off, Scale 60% off (applied to baseline).
- Burst multiplier: 2.5x baseline token price for usage beyond committed slab volume.
- Avg committed slab mix by ARR cohort: Starter 40%, Growth 45%, Scale 15% (by customer count among those who opt-in).
- Elasticity: delta slab uptake per 1ppt price change = 0.6ppt (observed from past promo cohort).
- Headcount cost per FTE (fully loaded annual): SWE infra $240k, SRE $220k, CS/AE $160k, Finance/BA $140k.
- Time-to-impact: 6–10 weeks to hire SWE/SRE, 4–6 weeks for CS/AE.

Scenarios (three):
1) Base case: slab uptake 18% of customers in Q4, slab discounts as above, burst 2.5x.
2) Upside: uptake 28% (promo + product placement), more customers in Growth tier; effective blended price improves 9% vs baseline.
3) Downside: uptake 8% (competitive pressure + macro), heavier burst usage; blended price falls 6% vs baseline.

Scenario outputs (monthly averages, normalized):
- Metric columns: effective token yield ($ per 1k tokens), blended gross margin (%), incremental gross contribution ($k/month), headcount delta (net new FTEs required or freezes).
- Base case: yield $0.052, margin 62.4%, incremental contribution +$420k/month, recommended hires +6 (3 SWE infra, 1 SRE, 2 CS).
- Upside: yield $0.058, margin 66.1%, incremental contribution +$860k/month, recommended hires +10 (6 SWE infra, 2 SRE, 2 CS).
- Downside: yield $0.048, margin 60.3%, incremental contribution -$95k/month (vs plan), recommended action hiring freeze and reallocate 2 infra offers to contracting.

Headcount phasing (quarter view):
- Week 1–4: open reqs for SWE infra x3, SRE x1, CS x2 (base). Hold SWE posting if downside triggers observed for 2 consecutive weeks of ARR softness.
- Week 5–10: ramp onboarding for SWE and CS. Measure real uptake after product placement campaign week 6; if uptake <12% then defer two SWE hires to contractor pools.

Trigger rules (operational):
- Green: weekly slab uptake rate >20% and net new committed ARR > target -> proceed with full hire cadence.
- Amber: uptake between 12%–20% -> proceed with CS and 50% of SWE hiring; postpone non-critical infra hires; increase sales incentives for Growth-tier migration.
- Red: uptake <12% for 2 consecutive weeks or burst volume > 55% of total usage -> immediate hiring freeze for SWE infra; shift budget to marketing incentives to drive slab migration.

Sensitivity waterfall (what moves margin most):
1) Uptake fraction of customers (largest).
2) Burst multiplier (if increased to 3x, downside mitigates but CS burden rises).
3) Discount depth on Growth tier (small changes have outsized effect on Scale economies).

Risk notes: 
- Cannibalization: early strong slab adoption by heavy users can increase burst usage beyond slab cap and reduce realized yield.
- Complexity: three-tier slab creates billing complexity; expect ~2–4% invoice disputes in first 2 quarters. Budget ~1.5 FTE of billing/ops support during launch.

Actions & next steps: 
- Finance to finalize sensitivity run with 1,000 Monte Carlo draws (input distributions for uptake, burst multiplier, and ARR churn) by 2027-02-10.
- Product to prepare Growth-tier in-console migration flow and AB test by 2027-02-18.
- Talent & Recruiting to create contractor pipeline for SWE infra contingency by 2027-02-25.
- Sales ops: define incentive accelerators for Growth-tier migration (AEs + CS) and run pilot on top 50 customers.

Notes & provenance: 
- Uptake elasticity parameter derived from promo cohort run in Nov 2026 (Confluence page linked).
- Headcount fully-loaded numbers include benefits, equity run-rate, and regional cost adjustments.
- This sheet is intentionally conservative on churn impact; evaluate stronger churn scenarios in the Monte Carlo pass.

Quick appendix: illustrative table (text format)
Cohort | # customers sample | assumed mean monthly tokens | expected slab uptake | effective yield ($/1k)
Starter | 2,400 | 120 | 12% | $0.050
Growth  | 620   | 980 | 28% | $0.044 (after deep discount but high committed volume)
Scale   | 45    | 80,000 | 6% | $0.026 (large commitment, large discount but stable)
